observation_summary: The Partial class throws an IllegalArgumentException or NullPointerException when adding fields, due to incorrect ordering logic and handling of unsupported duration fields.
hypothesis: The logic for comparing duration fields in Partial.java and UnsupportedDurationField.java is flawed. Specifically, the comparison logic fails to correctly handle cases where fields are unsupported or have null range duration types, leading to incorrect ordering validation and null pointer exceptions.
prediction: The fix will involve updating the comparison logic in UnsupportedDurationField to correctly handle supported fields and modifying the ordering validation in Partial to be more robust against null range duration types.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows changes to the comparison logic in UnsupportedDurationField and the ordering validation logic in Partial. These changes directly address the algorithmic steps used to validate the order of fields in a Partial object, confirming the issue is procedural.
reasoning_summary: The bug is caused by incorrect procedural logic in how duration fields are compared and validated within the Partial class. The fix involves rewriting the comparison strategy (in UnsupportedDurationField) and the validation logic (in Partial), which fits the definition of an Algorithm/Method defect. It is not a simple missing check (Checking) because the existing logic was fundamentally flawed in its comparison strategy, nor is it a design-level capability issue (Function/Class/Object).
evidence_used: The fix modifies the compareTo method in UnsupportedDurationField to change how unsupported fields are handled.
The fix modifies the ordering validation logic in Partial.java by removing an incorrect condition and adding a null check for range duration types.
The stack trace indicates an IllegalArgumentException during the validation of the types array in the Partial constructor.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds a null check, the root cause is the incorrect algorithmic approach to comparing duration fields, which is a procedural logic error rather than just a missing guard.
The fix does not require a design-level change or the addition of a new capability; it corrects the existing implementation of field ordering and comparison.
